newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds drifted lower on Friday evening in lifeless trade, after Thursday's mercurial market.
Weakness in foreign markets was considered the cause for more cautious trading in Bonos. But dealers remained positive saying they expect to see more gains in the week ahead.

"A target at 111 is likely in the coming days," a dealer said. Another added that the 10-year spread over German Bunds, which yesterday hit a record low at 143 bps, could slim even further toward the 100 level in the coming weeks. The December contract closed at 110.38, while the spread ended at 148.
Lower-than-expected October CPI data yesterday (0.1 percent month-on-month) convinced dealers that a fresh rate cut by the Bank of Spain was likely before year end.
"Some expect it will be December 13, others on December 24," a dealer said. "Everybody thinks the next cut will be around 25 basis points".
They added that an increase in prices in the shorter end of the yield curve was likely next week. The three year 7.80 percent bond closed at 109.86 from 110.01, yielding at 7.28 percent.
